title: Nanded, the last days
hook: tradition says he was stabbed by an assassin at Nanded and died of the wound

segments.voice: Yesterday, the white hawk and the blue horse: a sovereign bearing, kept alive in paintings and songs. Your line was the hawk and the horse.

A river in the south, the Godavari, far from Punjab. A town on its bank called Nanded. A great white gurdwara stands there now, and Sikhs travel a very long way to stand in it. Why so far from home? Because tradition says this is where the Tenth Guru's road ended. He had come south, a long way from Anandpur, and at Nanded he stopped. Sikhs tell what happened there gently, and that's how it's told here.
screen: `A RIVER IN THE SOUTH.` → `A TOWN CALLED NANDED.` → `WHERE THE ROAD ENDED.`

segments.voice: Tradition tells the last days in a few strokes. At Nanded, the Guru met an ascetic named Madho Das, living by the river. The meeting changed him. He became a Sikh, took the name Banda Singh, and the Guru sent him north to Punjab, a story for another day. Then came the blow. Tradition says an assassin, a Pathan, came near the Guru and stabbed him. The wound was dressed and stitched, and for a while it seemed he might recover. Then, the story goes, he drew a strong bow, and the stitches gave way. He knew his time was short. What he did with it is the part Sikhs hold closest. He did not name another person to follow him. Tradition says he gathered his Sikhs and placed the Guru's authority where it would stay; tomorrow looks at that carefully. Today, just notice the calm. A man who had lost his father, his mother and his four sons, who had fought and written and wandered, ends not in panic but in arranging what comes next. The place where he passed is now Takht Sachkhand Sri Hazur Sahib, one of the seats of authority in Sikh life. Sachkhand means the realm of truth, the last of the realms in Guru Nanak's Japji. So the name itself points past the earth. Nanded is where the line of human Gurus came to its close, and where a new way of being guided was about to begin.
screen: `MADHO DAS BECOMES BANDA SINGH.` · `THE ASSASSIN, AND THE WOUND.` · `CALM, ARRANGING WHAT COMES NEXT.` · `SACHKHAND: THE REALM OF TRUTH.` · then, large: `THE LAST DAYS.`

segments.voice: Let the bare outline of his life pass through your mind, the boy at Anandpur, the hawk, the letters, the losses, the long road south, the river at Nanded, and then let it go still. If you pray, sit in Waheguru for him; if not, sit in plain respect for a life given all the way to the end.
Nanded. The town on the Godavari where, tradition says, Guru Gobind Singh was wounded and passed, now home to Takht Sachkhand Sri Hazur Sahib. Today's word.
Your line: the last days. Not panic at the end, but calm. Rest gently tonight.
